When the canonical sample&#39;s steps content is absent (STEPS empty), the build passes and checkRegistered passes, because the registry entry and the Talk module still exist. Presentation.tsx then returns null because steps[index] is undefined, so no [data-step-count] element renders. verify.mjs render() waits 10s for that selector and throws Failure(&#39;render&#39;, &#39;route ... did not render a presentation&#39;, 0). That is a render timeout reported as phase=render, not a sample-phase check reporting the sample as missing or not matching the outline. The step-count and title/caption comparisons that would report phase=sample run only after the selector appears, so they are never reached. The review guidance includes &#39;steps content (titles, captions, steps) is absent&#39; in the definition of a missing sample. In scripts/verify.mjs, main() runs the build and then calls checkRegistered(slug) for the canonical sample before any browser work. If the registry has no entry for the slug, checkRegistered throws Failure(&#39;sample&#39;, &#39;... is not registered ...&#39;). If the entry&#39;s imported module does not exist, it throws a sample-phase Failure saying so. The top-level handler prints &#39;VERIFY FAILED phase=sample&#39; and calls process.exit(1). The outline is also checked in phase=sample. If the step count differs from the nine CANONICAL steps, that is a sample-phase Failure. If any step&#39;s title or caption differs from CANONICAL in order, that is a sample-phase Failure naming the step. tests/verify.e2e.test.ts runs verify.mjs on modified throwaway copies of the repo and asserts a non-zero exit plus the matching message. The faults cover an unregistered sample, a sample directory deleted and replaced by another reference, and out-of-order steps. Judge B argued that absent step content only produces a generic render timeout. That depends on emptying the steps array to zero entries, which is a constructed partial-deletion case. The guidance says not to construct those, and it credits a verifier that fails a missing sample with an explicit check reporting it as missing or not matching the outline, which this verifier has. Any steps that are removed, reordered, or retitled while the deck still renders hit the sample-phase count or title/caption checks. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-preview-readiness-bounded","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The contradiction does not hold. The clause in question requires that every wait for preview readiness has a timeout, and the one readiness wait in startPreview has one. It is a loop bounded by a 30,000 ms deadline. If the timeout passes or the child exits, it stops the preview and throws. The auditor&#39;s case depends on one fetch staying pending forever, which would need a server that accepts the connection but never answers. Nothing in the material shows that happening. The review guidance does not name a hanging request as a scenario, and the instructions say not to fail a criterion on a hypothetical input the guidance does not name. The guidance&#39;s failure case is a readiness wait with no timeout, and that is not what the code shows. The auditor also agrees the other two clauses are met: verify and inspect await the build before starting the preview, and readiness checks HTTP responses rather than parsing printed URLs, so the parsing clause does not apply. All three clauses are therefore met, and the pass verdict stands.","evidence":["In both copies of lib.mjs, startPreview sets const deadline = Date.now() + 30_000 and loops while Date.now() &lt; deadline. The loop breaks if the child has exited, and probes fetch(base + &#39;/&#39…","If the child process exits, the exited flag ends the loop. A fetch that never resolves would need a server that accepts the connection but never answers, and the material does not show that.","The guidance only fails a readiness wait that has no timeout. It does not name a per-request hang. Under the instructions, an unnamed hypothetical scenario does not make a fail.","verify.mjs main() awaits run(&#39;npm&#39;, [&#39;run&#39;, &#39;build&#39;]) and checks its exit code before renderAll calls startPreview. inspect-presentation.mjs also awaits the build before start…","Readiness is a fetch that checks res.ok and does not parse printed output, so the ANSI and chunking clause does not apply."],"citations":["scripts/lib.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3},{"id":"engineering-tests-isolate-resources","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The auditor describes the code correctly. In tests/continuity.e2e.test.ts, each test calls `await startPreview(REPO)` and then `await chromium.launch()` before entering its try/finally. A rejected launch would therefore skip preview.stop(). But that only happens if the browser fails to launch, and the code does not show that happening. This criterion&#39;s review guidance names two failure cases: two test files sharing a hardcoded port, and a test that kills only the npx wrapper and leaves the server running. It does not list browser launch failure here. It does list launch failure for the scripts criterion, engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exit. It also says a missing browser installation is not scored here, and that is the usual reason chromium.launch rejects. On the paths the tests actually run, every started process is stopped. startPreview picks a free port at runtime and starts vite detached. stop() sends SIGTERM to the whole process group, so the vite server is targeted, not an npm/npx wrapper. The finally blocks close the browser and stop the preview. So the stated gap does not overturn the pass.","evidence":["tests/continuity.e2e.test.ts: const preview = await startPreview(REPO) then const browser = await chromium.launch() before try { ... } finally { await browser.close(); preview.stop() }.
